overall: The AG found the Council violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating outside a meeting via a forwarded letter link, posting an insufficiently specific minutes notice, and approving insufficiently detailed roll call minutes; no intentional violation was found.

allegations.summary: Councilor forwarded a link to a letter to the Governor on shelter policy to fellow councilors, a quorum, allegedly deliberating outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: By forwarding the Letter to a quorum of the Council, the Councilor engaged in deliberation.

allegations.summary: Notice for the January 8, 2025 meeting listed only 'Approval of the minutes' without identifying which minutes would be approved.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Council posted notice which did not identify the minutes to be approved at the January 8, 2024, meeting, it violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: December 11, 2024 minutes recorded roll call votes only as tallies and did not list each councilor's vote by name, and did not list members present.
allegations.key_passage: Because the minutes of the December 11 Meeting fail to record the roll call votes by documenting the vote of each Council member, we find that the Council violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the violations were deliberate and willful and asked for a civil penalty against the Council.
allegations.key_passage: We do not find this violation to be intentional.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent.
Release of any written communication, including emails, between Councilors about the Letter.
Amend the December 11, 2024 minutes to record all roll call votes by documenting the vote of each Council member, and certify to the AG within 45 days.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
